_status: SUPERSEDED 2026-10-05 by compact server-side discovery. Preserve carr and the account connector; no machine config edits.
_finding: The CARR MCP Worker's `initialize` RPC (mcp-server/src/mcp.js) serves a ~200-word instructions block once per MCP server registration. This session's own tool list carries it TWICE, byte-identical, from the same backend (https://api.doctorcre.com/mcp), under two prefixes: mcp__carr__* (from the LOCAL ~/.claude.json config) and mcp__b36e17b6-7e3b-4e65-b890-21f21d538440__* (a claude.ai ACCOUNT-level connector, not a local file -- nothing on this Mac defines it).
~/.claude.json's only mcpServers entry, read (not written) to confirm this: {"carr": {"type": "http", "url": "https://api.doctorcre.com/mcp"}}. Every per-project mcpServers array checked was empty.
Measured cost: ~1,916 bytes (~547 tokens) per registration (ops/boot-budget-check.py measures and budgets exactly one instance); this session pays it twice, ~1,095 tokens total.
_historical_reason_against_actor_based_s: MCP's `initialize` is a per-connection handshake with no field meaning 'this is a second registration of a server you already introduced to this human this session.' The server DOES know the actor at initialize time (ctx.props), so it could cache 'has this actor already received the full block very recently' and serve a one-line pointer on a repeat -- but that cannot distinguish a genuine second registration (this case) from a genuinely NEW, independent session the same human opens moments later (a second terminal, a second device, a retried connection). Suppressing the full block on that legitimately-new session would silently withhold the one instruction that matters most: 'call standing-context FIRST.' A missed onboarding is worse than a duplicated one, and there is no safe threshold to tune this on -- so it stays a client-config fix, not a server heuristic.

_staged_fix.replacement: mcp-server/src/mcp.js advertises a compact core. list-verbs + call-verb preserve the complete registry on demand.
